children: The CAC 40 fell 0.4% to 8,095 on Thursday, extending losses from the previous session as investors remained cautious amid the lack of tangible progress in US-Iran talks.
Tensions remained elevated between the US and Iran as diplomatic talks showed little sign of a breakthrough, driving oil prices higher and keeping bond yields near multi-year highs.

Elsewhere, investors monitored the US-China trade truce after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the two economies had agreed to extend the agreement by two months, though Beijing has yet to confirm.
Domestically, the consumer confidence index held steady at 86 in September, exceeding the forecast of 85 but remaining well below its long-term average of 100.
Meanwhile, the manufacturing business climate indicator was unchanged at 101, matching August's revised reading but falling short of forecasts for 102.
Among the biggest decliners were BNP Paribas (-3.6%), STMicroelectronics (-1.3%), and Stellantis (-1.5%).

title: French Stocks Extend Losses
